newsitem.title: INDIA: Firemen battle India ONGC oil well fire.
newsitem.headline: Firemen battle India ONGC oil well fire.

text.p: Firemen battled for more than seven hours with a fire that broke out on Wednesday in an oil well developed by the Oil and Natural Gas Corp (ONGC) in India's southern Andhra Pradesh state, company officials said.

"The fire started around 1330 (0800 GMT). It is still on," said an official on duty at ONGC's control room set up at Rajahmundry, about 55 km (34 miles) from the site of the fire. "It has spread all around the site area."
He added that the fire covered a 3,000 square metre area.
State-run ONGC is India's largest oil exploration and drilling firm.
The official told Reuters the fire broke out in an oil well in the Mandapetta area, about 350 km (215 miles) east of the Andhra Pradesh capital Hyderabad.
"The drilling rig has collapsed. There are no casualties," the official said.
He said more than 250 people in nearby villages and those living in huts close to the well had been evacuated. The area near the well has been cordoned off, he said.

This was the second major blow-out in the state, which saw a fire rage for 62 days in a gas well in 1995. the fire was then brought under control with help from United States' International Well Control Inc. The well was later capped.
ONGC had then estimated losses worth 100 million rupees ($2.8 million) from wasted gas and 300 million rupees from damaged equipment.
ONGC drills in three districts in the state -- Krishna, East Godavari and West Godavari on the Bay of Bengal coast.
United News of India (UNI) said the blaze erupted on Wednesday during drilling, and flames leapt 55 feet (17 metres) in the air amid billowing clouds of smoke.
The official said there was no danger of the fire spreading as there were no wells adjacent to it.
The ONGC official said the fire broke out when a rig belonging to one of the contractors, Hi-Tech Drilling Services India Ltd, was active.
"We know Hi-Tech had drilled up to 2,754 metres when the blow out occurred," said the official. He said the well was targeted for a depth of about 4,000 metres.
"This area is a bit complicated. This looks like a high pressure pocket," he said.
The official said the company had been drilling for ONGC for the past two years and ONGC would offer every assistance to control the fire.
He said a senior ONGC official from New Delhi was leaving for the site of the well to assist local authorities.
